Travel-plan waits on it, returns 500/503s, and the UI passes that on to users.

Two things I checked and rejected as separate faults:
- **Network**: hubble drop counters match the normal period, so there is no connection-level fault.
- **Database tails in station, travel and user**: about 1–2% of their DB spans run long, and the same pattern appears on travel2 and order, which share the same MySQL. Nothing in those services' own work points to a separate injected fault, so I did not name them. A deeper MySQL-side check could still change this.
